Repo at /Users/harsh/agent-101/neatlogs-agent. I'm planning a minimal landing page for the product "Upshift" (recent commit: "Upshift: agent that fixes the code a version change breaks"). Breadth: medium. Report concisely:
1. What Upshift does (one-paragraph pitch), how it works step by step (pipeline/flow), key features — from README.md and the main source code.
2. The exact install/setup/run commands users need (from README, pyproject/package files, scripts, Makefile, CLI entrypoints) — quote them verbatim, including env vars / API keys needed and model providers supported (e.g. neatHack LiteLLM proxy).
3. The GitHub repo URL: run `git remote -v` (read-only) and report it.
4. Any existing web/frontend files, landing page, docs site, assets, logo, or brand colors in the repo (and whether assets/ is untracked). Check for any existing HTML/CSS, a docs/ or site/ folder, and how the demo/shop_app demo works (what the demo shows — e.g. before/after a version upgrade).
5. Sample terminal output of a run if documented (for an animated terminal demo on the landing page).
Do not modify anything.

content.content:
# Upshift

Dependabot opens the PR. Upshift makes it pass.

Upshift is an agent that fixes the code a version change breaks. Give it a Python repo and a package to
upgrade, or let it find the vulnerable ones. It researches the upgrade itself (changelog, release notes, migration guide, and an API diff
made by installing both versions), writes a playbook where every rule cites its source, bumps the
dependency, fixes the code one root cause at a time, and proves nothing new broke against the test
baseline it recorded before touching anything.

Built for #neatHack with neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai. Bring your own model key.

## Status

Package bumps, vulnerability scans and Python version upgrades work end to end. Third-party API drift
comes next.

## Run it

Needs Python 3.11+, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and the [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io/overview) with
its graph plugin (`entire plugin install graph`). Without Entire the agent still runs, but its graph tools and the
`entire graph verify` check report that they are unavailable.

```bash
uv sync
python3 scripts/check_secrets.py --install   # pre-commit hook that blocks committed keys
cp .env.example .env                         # fill in your provider and key (git-ignored)

# no model calls: clone, baseline, research, bump, and show what breaks
uv run upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --package pydantic --to 2 --dry-run

# the full agent
uv run upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --package pydantic --to 2
uv run upshift scan --repo demo/shop_app                     # find known vulnerabilities and fix each one
uv run upshift python --repo demo/shop_app --to 3.12         # move to a newer Python and fix what breaks
uv run upshift resume <run-id>     # continue a crashed or killed run
```

Runs live in `.upshift/runs/<run-id>/`: the working copy, its venv, `state.json`, the research sources and
the report. Playbooks are cached in `playbooks/` and reused by the next repo on the same upgrade.

## Models: bring your own key

Set `UPSHIFT_PROVIDER` and `UPSHIFT_MODEL` plus that provider's key in `.env` (read automatically,
never committed) or in your shell.

| `UPSHIFT_PROVIDER` | Needs | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `UPSHIFT_MODEL` defaults to `claude-opus-5-5`. Claude's thinking blocks are replayed unchanged and old tool results are trimmed by the API's context editing, so the conversation stays append-only |
| `azure-openai` | `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` | `UPSHIFT_MODEL` is the deployment name |
| `litellm` | `LITELLM_API_KEY` | A LiteLLM proxy. Defaults to the [neatHack model proxy](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/models) (Claude and Amazon Nova, e.g. `REDACTED.6`); set `LITELLM_BASE_URL` for your own |
| `openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Set `OPENAI_BASE_URL` for any OpenAI-compatible service (OpenRouter, Groq, Together, a local server) |
| `bedrock` | `UPSHIFT_AWS_PROFILE` | An explicit profile is required, so the default AWS account is never billed by accident |

The agent uses one message format internally and each provider translates to it, so adding a
provider means one adapter in `upshift/llm.py`. Every client is wrapped with `neatlogs.wrap`, so
model calls are traced with tokens and latency whichever provider you pick.

## How a job runs

| Phase | What happens | Where the tools come in |
|---|---|---|
| setup | Clone, create a venv, install, resolve the target version from PyPI | |
| baseline | Run the tests before changing anything | `entire graph verify --record-baseline` |
| bump | Rewrite the pins, install the new version, see what breaks | |
| research | Docs, changelog, GitHub release notes, API diff of both installed versions → cited playbook. Skipped for a security fix that breaks nothing | neatlogs `RETRIEVER`/`AGENT` spans |
| fix | One root cause per round. Progress is committed, regressions are reverted | `entire graph search / impact / explain` tools, one neatlogs span per round |
| verify | No new failures against the baseline, no old APIs left from the playbook; for security fixes, pip-audit again | `entire graph verify --pre-edit-baseline` |
| report | `UPSHIFT_REPORT.md` with changes, verification and sources | |

Every job is one neatlogs trace.

`upshift scan` installs the repo once, audits the exact installed versions with
[pip-audit](https://github.com/pypa/pip-audit) (OSV advisories, transitive dependencies included) and starts
one job per vulnerable package, like one PR each. The target is the smallest release that fixes every advisory,
preferring the current major line. A fix that breaks nothing is just a pin change with no model calls; one that
breaks the code goes through research and the fix loop like any other upgrade.

`upshift python` moves the version pins (`.python-version`, Dockerfile base image, GitHub Actions, tox, and
`requires-python` / ruff / mypy targets in pyproject.toml), rebuilds the venv on the new Python and fixes what
breaks. Its research is the Removed, Porting and Deprecated sections of each What's New page in range, plus a diff
of the standard library under both interpreters. If a pinned dependency has no release for the new Python, the job
stops and names it, so it can be upgraded first with `upshift bump`.

## Tests

```bash
uv run pytest
```

The fix-loop tests drive the real loop (repo, venv, pytest, git) with a scripted model in place of a real one.

version = "0.1.0"
description = "An agent that fixes the code a dependency or API version change breaks."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    "boto3>=1.35",
    "openai>=1.50",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "neatlogs>=0.8",
    "packaging>=24",
    "anthropic>=1.13.0",
]

[project.scripts]
upshift = "upshift.cli:main"

[dependency-groups]
dev = ["pytest>=8"]

[build-system]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]

# Model name. Anthropic defaults to claude-opus-5-5; for Azure OpenAI this is your deployment name.

# Upshift

Dependabot opens the PR. Upshift makes it pass.

Upshift is an agent that fixes the code a version change breaks. Give it a Python repo and a package to
upgrade, or let it find the vulnerable ones. It researches the upgrade itself (changelog, release notes, migration guide, and an API diff
made by installing both versions), writes a playbook where every rule cites its source, bumps the
dependency, fixes the code one root cause at a time, and proves nothing new broke against the test
baseline it recorded before touching anything.

Built for #neatHack with neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai. Bring your own model key.

## Status

Package bumps, vulnerability scans and Python version upgrades work end to end. Third-party API drift
comes next.

## Run it

Needs Python 3.11+, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and the [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io/overview) with
its graph plugin (`entire plugin install graph`). Without Entire the agent still runs, but its graph tools and the
`entire graph verify` check report that they are unavailable.

```bash
uv sync
python3 scripts/check_secrets.py --install   # pre-commit hook that blocks committed keys
cp .env.example .env                         # fill in your provider and key (git-ignored)

# no model calls: clone, baseline, research, bump, and show what breaks
uv run upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --package pydantic --to 2 --dry-run

# the full agent
uv run upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --package pydantic --to 2
uv run upshift scan --repo demo/shop_app                     # find known vulnerabilities and fix each one
uv run upshift python --repo demo/shop_app --to 3.12         # move to a newer Python and fix what breaks
uv run upshift resume <run-id>     # continue a crashed or killed run
```

Runs live in `.upshift/runs/<run-id>/`: the working copy, its venv, `state.json`, the research sources and
the report. Playbooks are cached in `playbooks/` and reused by the next repo on the same upgrade.

## Models: bring your own key

Set `UPSHIFT_PROVIDER` and `UPSHIFT_MODEL` plus that provider's key in `.env` (read automatically,
never committed) or in your shell.

| `UPSHIFT_PROVIDER` | Needs | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `UPSHIFT_MODEL` defaults to `claude-opus-5-5`. Claude's thinking blocks are replayed unchanged and old tool results are trimmed by the API's context editing, so the conversation stays append-only |
| `azure-openai` | `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` | `UPSHIFT_MODEL` is the deployment name |
| `litellm` | `LITELLM_API_KEY` | A LiteLLM proxy. Defaults to the [neatHack model proxy](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/models) (Claude and Amazon Nova, e.g. `REDACTED.6`); set `LITELLM_BASE_URL` for your own |
| `openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Set `OPENAI_BASE_URL` for any OpenAI-compatible service (OpenRouter, Groq, Together, a local server) |
| `bedrock` | `UPSHIFT_AWS_PROFILE` | An explicit profile is required, so the default AWS account is never billed by accident |

The agent uses one message format internally and each provider translates to it, so adding a
provider means one adapter in `upshift/llm.py`. Every client is wrapped with `neatlogs.wrap`, so
model calls are traced with tokens and latency whichever provider you pick.

## How a job runs

| Phase | What happens | Where the tools come in |
|---|---|---|
| setup | Clone, create a venv, install, resolve the target version from PyPI | |
| baseline | Run the tests before changing anything | `entire graph verify --record-baseline` |
| bump | Rewrite the pins, install the new version, see what breaks | |
| research | Docs, changelog, GitHub release notes, API diff of both installed versions → cited playbook. Skipped for a security fix that breaks nothing | neatlogs `RETRIEVER`/`AGENT` spans |
| fix | One root cause per round. Progress is committed, regressions are reverted | `entire graph search / impact / explain` tools, one neatlogs span per round |
| verify | No new failures against the baseline, no old APIs left from the playbook; for security fixes, pip-audit again | `entire graph verify --pre-edit-baseline` |
| report | `UPSHIFT_REPORT.md` with changes, verification and sources | |

Every job is one neatlogs trace.

`upshift scan` installs the repo once, audits the exact installed versions with
[pip-audit](https://github.com/pypa/pip-audit) (OSV advisories, transitive dependencies included) and starts
one job per vulnerable package, like one PR each. The target is the smallest release that fixes every advisory,
preferring the current major line. A fix that breaks nothing is just a pin change with no model calls; one that
breaks the code goes through research and the fix loop like any other upgrade.

`upshift python` moves the version pins (`.python-version`, Dockerfile base image, GitHub Actions, tox, and
`requires-python` / ruff / mypy targets in pyproject.toml), rebuilds the venv on the new Python and fixes what
breaks. Its research is the Removed, Porting and Deprecated sections of each What's New page in range, plus a diff
of the standard library under both interpreters. If a pinned dependency has no release for the new Python, the job
stops and names it, so it can be upgraded first with `upshift bump`.

## Tests

```bash
uv run pytest
```

"""upshift bump --repo PATH_OR_URL --package NAME [--to VERSION]
upshift scan --repo PATH_OR_URL
upshift python --repo PATH_OR_URL --to 3.12
upshift resume RUN_ID"""

import argparse
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from . import pipeline, pyversion, tracing, vuln
from .llm import LLMConfigError
from .state import RunState


def load_env_file(path: Path = Path(".env")) -> None:
    """Read KEY=VALUE lines from a git-ignored .env. Variables already set in the shell win."""
    if not path.exists():
        return
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, value = line.split("=", 1)
        value = value.strip().strip("\"'")
        if value:  # an empty OPENAI_BASE_URL= would otherwise override the SDK default
            os.environ.setdefault(key.removeprefix("export ").strip(), value)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    load_env_file()
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="upshift", description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    bump = sub.add_parser("bump", help="upgrade a package and fix what breaks")
    bump.add_argument("--repo", required=True, help="local path or git URL")
    bump.add_argument("--package", required=True)
    bump.add_argument("--to", help="target version or prefix (default: latest stable)")
    bump.add_argument("--python", help="Python for the project's venv (default: its .python-version, else 3.12)")
    bump.add_argument("--fresh-research", action="store_true",
                      help="ignore a cached playbook and research the upgrade again")
    bump.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                      help="no model calls: set up, baseline, gather research, bump, show what breaks")

    scan = sub.add_parser("scan", help="audit dependencies for known vulnerabilities and fix each one")
    scan.add_argument("--repo", required=True, help="local path or git URL")
    scan.add_argument("--python", help="Python for the project's venv (default: its .python-version, else 3.12)")
    scan.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                      help="no model calls: fixes that break nothing still complete; others stop after research")

    py = sub.add_parser("python", help="move the project to a newer Python and fix what breaks")
    py.add_argument("--repo", required=True, help="local path or git URL")
    py.add_argument("--to", required=True, help="target Python, e.g. 3.12")
    py.add_argument("--from", dest="from_version", help="current Python (default: the repo's .python-version)")
    py.add_argument("--fresh-research", action="store_true",
                    help="ignore a cached playbook and research the upgrade again")
    py.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                    help="no model calls: set up, baseline, move to the new Python, show what breaks")

    resume = sub.add_parser("resume", help="continue a run from its last completed phase")
    resume.add_argument("run_id")
    resume.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    stamp = time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
    jobs = []
    if args.command in ("bump", "scan"):
        args.python = args.python or pyversion.detect(args.repo) or "3.12"
    if args.command == "python":
        state = RunState(run_id=f"{stamp}-python-{args.to}", kind="python", source=args.repo, package="python",
                         wanted=args.to, python=args.from_version or "", fresh_research=args.fresh_research)
        state.save()
        jobs, tags = [state], ["python", args.to]
    elif args.command == "bump":
        state = RunState(run_id=f"{stamp}-{args.package.lower()}", kind="bump", source=args.repo,
                         package=args.package, wanted=args.to, python=args.python,
                         fresh_research=args.fresh_research)
        state.save()
        jobs, tags = [state], [state.kind, state.package]
    elif args.command == "resume":
        state = RunState.load(args.run_id)
        jobs, tags = [state], [state.kind, state.package]
    else:
        tags = ["vuln"]

    tracing.init(tags)
    try:
        if args.command == "scan":
            jobs = vuln.scan(args.repo, args.python, stamp)
            if not jobs:
                print("[upshift] nothing to fix")
        results = [run_job(state, args.dry_run) for state in jobs]
    except LLMConfigError as exc:
        print(f"[upshift] {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    finally:
        tracing.shutdown()
    return 0 if all(results) else 1


def run_job(state: RunState, dry_run: bool) -> bool:
    print(f"[upshift] run {state.run_id} → {state.dir}")
    state = pipeline.run(state, dry_run=dry_run)
    if state.result:
        print(f"[upshift] {'OK' if state.result['ok'] else 'INCOMPLETE'}: "
              f"{state.result['passed']} passing, {len(state.result['new_failures'])} new failures. "
              f"Report: {state.dir / pipeline.REPORT}")
    return bool(state.result.get("ok")) or dry_run


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Here's what's in the repo for the Upshift landing page. All paths are under `/Users/harsh/agent-101/neatlogs-agent`. I didn't change anything.

## 1. What Upshift does

**Pitch** (README tagline: *"Dependabot opens the PR. Upshift makes it pass."*; the asset uses *"Your deps move. Your code keeps up."*):
Upshift is an agent that fixes the code a version change breaks. You give it a Python repo and a package to upgrade, or let it find the vulnerable ones. It researches the upgrade itself: changelog, release notes, the migration guide, and an API diff made by installing both versions. From that it writes a playbook where every rule cites its source. Then it bumps the dependency and fixes the code one root cause at a time. Finally it proves nothing new broke, against the test results it recorded before touching anything. It was built for #neatHack with neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai, and you bring your own model key.

**Pipeline** (README "How a job runs"; `upshift/pipeline.py`):
1. **setup**: clone the repo, create a venv, install, resolve the target version from PyPI.
2. **baseline**: run the tests before changing anything (`entire graph verify --record-baseline`).
3. **bump**: rewrite the pins, install the new version, see what breaks.
4. **research**: docs, changelog, GitHub release notes and an API diff produce the cited playbook. This step is skipped for a security fix that breaks nothing.
5. **fix**: one root cause per round. Progress is committed and regressions are reverted. Uses the `entire graph search / impact / explain` tools.
6. **verify**: no new failures against the baseline and no old APIs left from the playbook. Security fixes run pip-audit again.
7. **report**: writes `UPSHIFT_REPORT.md` with the changes, verification and sources.

Every job is one neatlogs trace.

**Key features:**
- **Three commands:**
  - `bump`: upgrade a package.
  - `scan`: pip-audit/OSV, including transitive dependencies. It picks the smallest release that fixes every advisory, one job per package. A fix that breaks nothing is just a pin change with no model calls.
  - `python`: moves the Python pins in `.python-version`, the Dockerfile, GitHub Actions, tox and pyproject.
- `resume` continues a crashed run, and `--dry-run` makes no model calls.
- Playbooks are cached in `playbooks/` and reused (pydantic 1→2, jinja2 2.11→3.1, Python 3.10→3.12).
- A pre-commit secrets hook blocks committed keys.
- Every model client is wrapped with neatlogs tracing.
- **Roadmap:** "Third-party API drift comes next." The asset calls this `upshift watch`. It is not implemented in `cli.py`.

**Measured cost per job** (from `business/cfo-inputs.md`):
- requests security fix: $0
- jinja2 security fix: about $0.07
- pydantic 1→2: $0.33
- Python 3.10→3.12: about $0.51

## 2. Install and run commands (verbatim from README)

Requirements: Python 3.11+, uv, and the Entire CLI with its graph plugin (`entire plugin install graph`). Without Entire the agent still runs, but the graph tools report themselves unavailable. The CLI entrypoint is `upshift = "upshift.cli:main"`.

```bash
uv sync
python3 scripts/check_secrets.py --install   # pre-commit hook that blocks committed keys
cp .env.example .env                         # fill in your provider and key (git-ignored)

# no model calls: clone, baseline, research, bump, and show what breaks
uv run upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --package pydantic --to 2 --dry-run

# the full agent
uv run upshift bump --repo demo/shop_app --package pydantic --to 2
uv run upshift scan --repo demo/shop_app                     # find known vulnerabilities and fix each one
uv run upshift python --repo demo/shop_app --to 3.12         # move to a newer Python and fix what breaks
uv run upshift resume <run-id>     # continue a crashed or killed run
```

Tests: `uv run pytest`.

Extra CLI flags: `--python`, `--fresh-research`, and `--from` (on the `python` command).

**Model providers** (set `UPSHIFT_PROVIDER` and `UPSHIFT_MODEL` in `.env` or your shell):

| `UPSHIFT_PROVIDER` | Needs | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `UPSHIFT_MODEL` defaults to `claude-opus-5-5` |
| `azure-openai` | `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` | `OPENAI_API_VERSION=2024-10-21`; the model is the deployment name |
| `litellm` | `LITELLM_API_KEY` | Defaults to the neatHack proxy (https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/models); `LITELLM_BASE_URL` for your own proxy |
| `openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `OPENAI_BASE_URL` for OpenRouter, Groq, Together or a local server |
| `bedrock` | `UPSHIFT_AWS_PROFILE` | `UPSHIFT_AWS_REGION=us-west-2`; an explicit profile is required |

- The neatHack proxy models are `claude-opus-4.6`, `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-haiku`, `nova-pro`, `nova-lite`, `nova-2-lite` and `nova-micro` (e.g. `REDACTED.6`).
- Optional: `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` (without it, spans are created but not exported) and `UPSHIFT_AGENT_VERSION=v0`.

## 3. GitHub repo

`git remote -v` shows `origin https://harsh-madhav@github.com/harsh-madhav/upshift.git` for both fetch and push. The public URL is **https://github.com/harsh-madhav/upshift**.

## 4. Existing web files, assets and brand

- There is no `docs/` or `site/` folder, no landing page, and no favicon or SVG logo.
- The only HTML is `assets/upshift-tools.html`, a 2000x1125 slide/poster, plus its render `assets/upshift-tools.png`. `assets/` is **untracked**: it's in `.gitignore` and was removed from git in commit 235c416.
- **Brand tokens** from that HTML's `:root`:
  - Colours: `--paper #F1F2EE`, `--ink #0D0D0D`, `--soft #55585E`, `--rule #C9CBC6`, `--blue #2D5BFF`, `--blue-tint #E3E9FF`, `--green #0E9A62`, `--yellow #FFD12E`, `--red #E5484D`, `--white #FFFFFF`
  - Fonts: **Archivo** (variable wdth/wght, display, weight 800–900, font-stretch 108–112%) and **JetBrains Mono**, both from Google Fonts.
- **Wordmark:** a 50px black rounded square with a yellow "↑" glyph, then "upshift" in Archivo 800, then a pill badge "#neatHack".
- **Poster copy you can reuse:**
  - Three triggers: `upshift scan` (VULN), `upshift bump` (ASK), `upshift watch` (DRIFT)
  - Loop: Research → Playbook → Fix → Verify → Recover → PR + report
  - Partner panels: neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai
  - Footer: "#neatHack · Oct 10–12, 2026"

**The demo app** (`demo/shop_app/`) is a small shop with orders, receipts and settings, deliberately pinned to old versions so each upgrade breaks something:
- **pydantic 1.10.13** in `shop/models.py` and `shop/orders.py`: `constr(regex=)`, `validator`, `root_validator`, `orm_mode`, `parse_obj`, `.dict()`. Upgrading to 2.14.0 makes the suite fail at import; after the fix all 16 tests pass and only models/orders changed.
- **jinja2 2.11.3** in `shop/receipts.py`: `Markup`, `escape`, `contextfilter`, `environmentfilter`. The 3.1.6 security fix covers 4 CVEs; Upshift moved the imports to markupsafe and switched to `pass_context`/`pass_environment`, and all 21 tests pass.
- **requests 2.31.0**: 3 CVEs, fixed by a pin change only, with no model calls.
- **Python 3.10** (`.python-version`, Dockerfile, CI): `shop/settings.py` uses `SafeConfigParser`, `distutils.strtobool` and `inspect.getargspec`. Moving to 3.12, Upshift produced `ConfigParser`, a local `strtobool` and `getfullargspec`; all 26 tests pass.
- **Untracked work in progress:** `shop/payments.py`, `tests/acme_sandbox.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_payments.py` and `scripts/traffic.py`, plus a modification to `shop/orders.py`. This is the API-drift demo. A fake "acme" payments API v1 sends `Deprecation`/`Sunset` headers ("Sat, 31 Oct 2026") and returns 410 after sunset, and the migration target is v2 `/v2/payments`. Traffic is logged to `logs/app.log` and traced in neatlogs. That feature isn't implemented yet.
